definition: Google Clips is a discontinued miniature clip-on camera device developed by Google..
details: Google Clips is a discontinued miniature clip-on camera device developed by Google.

explainer.lead: Google Clips was a miniature clip-on camera developed by Google. Its small, attachable form made it a different kind of personal camera, though the product has since been discontinued.

tiers.eli5: Imagine a tiny camera that fastens on with a clip instead of needing to be carried like a big camera. That was Google Clips: a small Google-made device for taking pictures. It is no longer a current product.
tiers.practitioner: Treat Google Clips as discontinued camera hardware, not as a software library, API, or trainable model. Its defining engineering characteristics are its miniature size and clip-on form; current support, interfaces, and capture settings should not be assumed.
tiers.paperLevel: Google Clips is formally a discontinued miniature clip-on camera device developed by Google. This description identifies a hardware product rather than a specified AI architecture, algorithm, or research method.

explainer.example: A person clips Google Clips to a jacket before a family picnic, points it toward the group, and captures a picture without holding a full-size camera.
explainer.intuition: The idea is to shrink a camera into a small accessory that can be clipped on, making the way it is carried and positioned part of the product design.
howItWorks: Clip the miniature camera onto a suitable surface or item of clothing.
Position it so the camera faces the scene of interest.
Use the camera to capture a picture.
explainer.whyItMatters: Google Clips illustrates how miniaturization and a clip-on design can change a camera from something carried in the hand into a small personal accessory. Its discontinued status also means it should be discussed as a past product rather than a current option.
misconceptions: It is a physical camera, not a photography app.
Its name does not make it a video-clip editing tool.
It is discontinued, not a currently active Google product.
